findings.claim: SPDR Gold Trust is a New York investment trust sponsored by World Gold Trust Services, LLC, with The Bank of New York Mellon as trustee and HSBC Bank plc and JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as custodians, and its objective is for the shares to reflect the price of gold bullion less the trust's expenses.
findings.source_title: SPDR Gold Trust Form 10-K for the year ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: At September 30, 2026 the trust held 33,996.7 thousand ounces of gold with a market value of $141,980,319 thousand at an LBMA Gold Price PM of $4,176.30, up from 32,528.2 thousand ounces worth $124,430,281 thousand at $3,825.30 a year earlier.
findings.source_title: SPDR Gold Trust Form 10-K for the year ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: NAV per share rose from $352.09 to $382.88 in the fiscal year ended September 30, 2026, a total return of 8.74% at NAV and 7.14% at market value, compared with 44.89% and 46.25% in fiscal 2025.
findings.source_title: SPDR Gold Trust Form 10-K for the year ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: Fiscal 2026 net income was $10,764,495 thousand versus $35,553,538 thousand in fiscal 2025, and included a $(10,398,959) thousand change in unrealized gain on gold, offset by a $21,540,436 thousand realized gain on gold distributed for redemptions.
findings.source_title: SPDR Gold Trust Form 10-K for the year ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: In fiscal 2026, 155,400 thousand shares were created for 14,314.9 thousand ounces and 139,000 thousand shares were redeemed for 12,715.1 thousand ounces, taking shares outstanding from 353,700 thousand to 370,100 thousand, while 131.3 thousand ounces were sold to pay expenses.
findings.source_title: SPDR Gold Trust Form 10-K for the year ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: Shares outstanding were 361,800,000 on November 23, 2026, down from 370,100,000 at September 30, 2026, implying net redemptions of about 8.3 million shares after fiscal year end.
findings.source_title: SPDR Gold Trust Form 10-K for the year ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: The trust's only recurring fixed expense is the sponsor fee, accruing at 0.40% of daily NAV, and sponsor fees were $598,191,851.95 for the year ended September 30, 2026.
findings.source_title: SPDR Gold Trust Form 10-K for the year ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: For the three months ended June 30, 2026, NAV total return was -12.72% as NAV per share fell from $423.34 to $369.47, and the LBMA Gold Price PM ended the quarter at $4,026.05 after a period high of $5,405.00 on January 29, 2026.
findings.source_title: SPDR Gold Trust Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026

findings.claim: The trust indenture does not authorize borrowing to pay ordinary expenses, the trust holds no derivatives or long-term debt, and it holds no cash because gold is sold monthly to pay expenses.
findings.source_title: SPDR Gold Trust Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026

findings.claim: The FY2026 10-K repeats the risk that if LBMA Good Delivery Rules or the Good Delivery List change materially or lose acceptance, the trust may be unable to accept gold for creations or deliver gold for redemptions.
findings.source_title: SPDR Gold Trust Form 10-K for the year ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: The FY2026 10-K says tariffs, export or import restrictions, sanctions and other trade barriers could disrupt cross-border gold trade, raise transport and trading costs and increase volatility, with either positive or negative effects on the gold price.
findings.source_title: SPDR Gold Trust Form 10-K for the year ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: The FY2026 10-K says the premium or discount of the shares to NAV may widen after the COMEX close at 1:30 PM New York time because the shares trade on NYSE Arca until 8:00 PM when gold-market liquidity is lower.
findings.source_title: SPDR Gold Trust Form 10-K for the year ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: The FY2025 Form 10-K states that gain recognized by an individual U.S. shareholder on shares held more than one year is treated as gain on collectibles, taxed at a maximum federal rate of 28% rather than 20%.
findings.source_title: SPDR Gold Trust Form 10-K for the year ended September 30, 2025

findings.claim: As of October 31, 2026, SSGA reported a one-year NAV return of -2.84% and a year-to-date NAV return of -9.46%, compared with LBMA Gold Price PM returns of -2.45% and -10.41%.
findings.source_title: SSGA fund page for SPDR Gold Shares (GLD)

findings.claim: World Gold Council data for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 show central banks and other official institutions bought 321.2 tonnes of gold, up 42% year over year, physically backed gold ETFs added 211.2 tonnes, and the average LBMA gold price was $4,262.2 per ounce, down from $4,506.3 in the prior quarter.
findings.source_title: World Gold Council Gold Demand Trends Q3 2026

findings.claim: Bureau Veritas completed the annual full bar count of the trust's gold at the HSBC London vault and the JPMorgan London and New York vaults on September 30, 2026, after random sample counts on March 17 and 18, 2026.
findings.source_title: SPDR Gold Trust Form 10-K for the year ended September 30, 2026

upcoming_catalysts.event: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 31, 2026, the first quarterly report of fiscal 2027.
World Gold Council outlook that central-bank buying is likely to at least match 2025 after a strong third quarter, which would support the gold price GLD tracks after expenses.

policy_links.policy: Internal Revenue Code treatment of gold and interests in gold-holding trusts as collectibles, with a maximum 28% long-term capital-gains rate for individual shareholders
policy_links.bottleneck: after-tax return to taxable individual holders
policy_links.revenue_mechanism: The rule does not create revenue for the trust. It raises the federal tax rate on an individual shareholder's long-term gain from selling shares or from gold the trust sells.

policy_links.policy: People's Bank of China continued reported official gold purchases, adding 63 tonnes in the third quarter of 2026
policy_links.revenue_mechanism: Official purchases can support the LBMA gold price that sets GLD's NAV, but the World Gold Council report does not identify purchases of GLD shares or any payment to the trust.

key_risks.risk: GLD's value is the gold price minus expenses. NAV fell 12.72% in the quarter ended June 30, 2026, the one-year NAV return was -2.84% as of October 31, 2026, and fiscal 2026 net income fell about 70% as unrealized gains on gold shrank by $10.4 billion.

Creations, redemptions, custody and orderly trading depend on continued market acceptance of LBMA Good Delivery standards. A break in those standards could stop the creation mechanism and open a large premium or discount to NAV.
The 0.40% sponsor fee, $598 million in fiscal 2026, is paid by selling gold, so gold per share declines even if the gold price is unchanged, and the trust has no yield.
All of the gold is held by two custodians, HSBC and JPMorgan, so a custody or sub-custody failure would hit the entire asset pool.

notes: GLD is a grantor trust that holds allocated gold, not an operating company, so there is no earnings guidance, debt maturity or share offering in the corporate sense. Basket creations and redemptions are in-kind exchanges for gold and are not dilution. The FY2026 Form 10-K was filed November 24, 2026 (accession 0001437749-26-038190) and replaces the 10-Q as the main source here. The 10-K's Item 3 Legal Proceedings section has no content in the fetched text, so no proceedings were identified. The post-year-end net redemption figure is an inference from the September 30 and November 23 share counts. The SSGA return figures are as of October 31, 2026 and were not refreshed; the FY2026 10-K does not give an October or November NAV. World Gold Council ETF-flow figures are for the global physically backed category and are not a GLD-only number. No going-concern language was found.
